name: Jahath
overview: Jahath was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as a Gershonite, descended from Gershon, son of Levi. He is uniquely noted as the son of Libni, situating him within the Levitical genealogies. His role is connected to the priestly divisions of Israel, as indicated by his tribal affiliation and family lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Jahath means 'snatch up' and is a proper name recorded in Scripture. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it carries a meaning that may reflect characteristics or roles associated with the individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jahath as the son of Libni. It is also inferred that Zimmah was his father, placing Jahath within a clear Levitical family line. No other family relationships are documented beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Jahath's significance lies in his place within the Levitical genealogies, which were essential for organizing the priestly and temple duties among the Israelites. As a Gershonite and son of Libni, he represents one of the key family branches responsible for the service of the tabernacle. His mention in 1 Chronicles 6:20 highlights the importance of maintaining accurate records of Levitical heritage for the proper administration of worship in Israel.
